finding: Projects and subgroups cannot be more visible than their parent group.
ara_relevance: Direct precedent for a visibility ceiling.
limitation: GitLab prevents making a parent private while public descendants exist; ARA proposes cascading effective restriction.

finding: Every parent must allow a permission; effective permissions are intersections of guardrails and grants.
ara_relevance: Precedent for maximum inherited authority.
limitation: Applies to cloud accounts rather than derived educational artifacts.

finding: Effective access can be the intersection of identity policies and organizational control policies; explicit deny overrides.
ara_relevance: Supports materialized effective-audience reasoning.
limitation: ARA has a much smaller public/private surface.

finding: Requested and issued scope must be equal to or less than the originally granted scope.
ara_relevance: Direct precedent for non-amplifying delegation.
limitation: Token scopes are temporary credentials, not provenance nodes.

finding: Refresh requests cannot include scope not originally granted.
ara_relevance: Widely adopted scope attenuation rule.
limitation: Does not define ancestor graphs or content derivation.

finding: Delegated credentials gain caveats that attenuate where, by whom and for what they can be used.
ara_relevance: Strong conceptual match for descendants adding restrictions only.
limitation: Cryptographic bearer credentials are not required for the ARA model.

source: Protecting privacy using the Decentralized Label Model
finding: Owners attach policies to information and decentralized information-flow control preserves them through processing.
ara_relevance: Precedent for owner restrictions following information.
limitation: ARA needs a simpler application-level model.

source: A Policy Framework for Data Fusion and Derived Data Control
finding: Studies restrictions on access and use of information derived from multiple sources.
ara_relevance: Directly relevant to multiple parents and policy composition.
limitation: Requires adaptation to versioned learning artifacts.

finding: Uniform relationship and ACL data model at trillions of ACLs and millions of checks per second.
ara_relevance: Shows relational authorization can scale.
limitation: ARA should not reproduce Zanzibar complexity prematurely.

finding: Documents public access, parent-child objects and multiple restrictions.
ara_relevance: Practical modeling reference for users, groups and ancestors.
limitation: Implementation choice remains open.

finding: Represents derivation chains, generation activities and responsible agents.
ara_relevance: Provides vocabulary for version provenance.
limitation: Needs ARA-specific specialization and UX terms.

finding: Commits, trees and blobs are immutable objects; commits reference parent IDs and snapshots.
ara_relevance: Primary precedent for immutable content-addressed revision DAGs.
limitation: ARA requires pedagogical semantics and access edges beyond Git.

finding: Defines the commit graph as a directed acyclic graph formed by linked commits.
ara_relevance: Supports visible version graph terminology.
limitation: Git vocabulary need not be exposed publicly.

finding: Manages pointers and metadata over underlying object stores with Git-like commits, branches and history.
ara_relevance: Direct precedent for version semantics over object storage.
limitation: Data-lake system; not a BaaS or learning platform.

finding: Zero-copy branch creation is metadata-only; new versions appear only for changed objects.
ara_relevance: Supports economical derivations without full copying.
limitation: ARA still needs fine-grained access and offline study.

finding: Advocates local work, offline capability, collaboration, ownership and long-term preservation.
ara_relevance: Supports IndexedDB-first editing and later sync.
limitation: Does not prescribe checkpoint or access semantics.

finding: Append-only events improve auditability but impose major complexity; selective adoption is recommended.
ara_relevance: Supports operation log without requiring full event sourcing.
limitation: ARA should keep revisions as editorial source and events as provenance.

finding: Precomputed views support efficient queries over data that is expensive to derive repeatedly.
ara_relevance: Supports effective-access and history projections for front-end.
limitation: Views add storage and consistency trade-offs.

finding: Nodes may call callbacks or open links.
ara_relevance: Suitable for clickable small graphs and prototypes.
limitation: Rich interaction requires relaxed security setting and larger graphs need evaluation.

finding: Full JavaScript graph visualization and analysis library with layouts, traversal, compound graphs and viewport operations.
ara_relevance: Strong candidate for investigative graph browsing.
limitation: Requires custom UX and performance prototype.

finding: Interactive node-edge component with custom nodes, selection and viewport controls.
ara_relevance: Strong candidate when nodes contain authoring controls.
limitation: Graph analysis and layout require complements.

finding: Provides layered and other graph layout algorithms in JavaScript and Web Workers.
ara_relevance: Useful for directional DAG layout with another renderer.
limitation: Not a renderer or complete UI.
